title: Ossoff holds Georgia and Cooper flips North Carolina in early Senate calls
dek: Election night is moving fast and the count is far from done. Two early Senate calls favour Democrats, and the posts about them read very differently depending on who is posting.
what: Decision Desk HQ, a results service, posted on X at 7:18 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday 3 November that it projects Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff wins the Georgia Senate race. CBS News reports that it also projected Ossoff the winner, over Republican Representative Mike Collins, and that the win keeps a Democratic seat and the party's hopes of a Senate majority alive. The outlets give different times for their calls, and I have not matched them to the minute.

The Associated Press projects, as reported by Yahoo News, that former governor Roy Cooper won North Carolina's Senate race over Republican Michael Whatley, flipping a seat held by Republicans. NPR and CNBC headline the same two results. The Cooper win is the first Democratic Senate win in North Carolina since 2008, a point also made by the aggregator PopBase in its post.

CNBC's election desk says the House is leaning Democratic, with at least 205 seats for Democrats and at least 160 for Republicans so far. It calls the Texas Senate race, between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton, "leaning" Democratic as of 9 p.m. Eastern, which is not a call. CNBC also notes that North Carolina's count was delayed by extended voting hours, that ballot scanning problems were reported in Westchester County, New York, and that an Alaska race is under a Justice Department investigation with results pending.
Control of the Senate and the House has not been decided. These are early projections on election night, and counts will change. I could not confirm any final totals.
why: The first calls came within minutes of polls closing and landed in a night when both parties' accounts were already posting about turnout and polling place problems. Winning posts are quick to share and easy to read in more than one way.

worlds.name: Posters treating the calls as a Democratic wave
worlds.sees: Georgia held and North Carolina flipped, so the Senate is in play. The post carries the Cooper news itself.

worlds.name: Posters alarmed by the calls
worlds.sees: One poster calls the night "a blue tsunami" and "horrifying", although votes are still being counted.

common: Established: Decision Desk HQ, CBS News and the Associated Press (as reported by Yahoo News) project Ossoff the winner in Georgia and Cooper the winner in North Carolina. Not established: who controls the Senate or the House, the Texas result, and any final margin. The "blue tsunami" post is one poster's judgement about a night that was not over when it was written; no outlet cited here says the outcome is settled.
next: Remaining Senate calls, the Texas result, and the House count as later results arrive.
